_doc: Culinary-to-Federal crosswalk: Cost Index ingredient slugs -> US Census HS6 import commodity codes. Every code is VERIFIED against the Census I_COMMODITY_SDESC returned in data/census-imports.jsonl (the description must match the ingredient). US Census general-imports data is public domain. HS6 is the finest public aggregation; some codes combine related items or a single form (fresh/frozen) — noted. This is a descriptive reference of the US import stream — never a delivered/retail price, never import VOLUME (quantity is not published at HS6), never a forecast.
_source: US Census Bureau, International Trade, general imports by HS6 (api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade/imports/hs). Public domain.

_pending.resolved_2026_07: whole-salmon (030214), whole-halibut (030221) and whole-trout (030211) are now mapped and SDESC-verified.
_pending.captured_not_tracked: mussels — SDESC-verified US import streams were pulled for both forms (030731 live/fresh, 030732 frozen) and kept in data/census-imports.jsonl for provenance, but mussels is not one of the 100 tracked ingredients, so no slug is attached; add a mapping only if mussels is ever added as a tracked ingredient (it needs its own yield/pricing spine too).
_pending.hs10_cut_level_2026_07: Beef and pork now map at HS10 (US statistical primal level, from 2017): ribeye = rib primal (0201305025 + frozen 0202305025), striploin + beef-tenderloin = loin primal (…5045), ground-beef = boneless-NESOI trim (…5085), pork-belly = fresh bellies (0203194010), pork-shoulder = bone-in shoulder + frozen ham/shoulder. Aggregated fresh+frozen per cut by the builder.
_pending.deliberately_unmapped: Left without an import code on purpose: short-rib is not isolable at HS10 (it spans the chuck/plate/rib primals); pork-loin has no loin-specific pork line (stays on the frozen-cuts NESOI); the fresh herbs other than cilantro (basil, parsley, dill, mint, oregano, rosemary, tarragon, thyme) have no HS10 line of their own; chicken and turkey are domestic-dominant and their import streams misrepresent the tracked cuts; vegetable-oil is a blend with no single HS code. Absence here is a deliberate honesty choice, not missing work.
_pending.note: The import field is populated only for ingredients with a genuine, SDESC-verified US import stream. Where HS6 combines several tracked items under one code (peppers, lettuces, brassicas, squash, pork cuts...), the shared stream is attached to each with a 'combines / not split' note — descriptive supply context, never a per-item delivered price or volume.
_pending.hs10_produce_2026_07: Produce mapped to its finest HS10 level: peppers split bell (HS8 07096040) / jalapeño / serrano / poblano / habanero-as-chili-NESOI; squash into zucchini/butternut/acorn/yellow (org+non-org summed); the brassica basket into cabbage/broccoli/bok-choy/kale/napa/collard; lettuce into romaine/butterhead/red+green (iceberg stays head lettuce); blueberries exclude cranberries and raspberries exclude blackberries; green-onion & leek split; snow-peas and green-beans isolated; and three breadth wins — cilantro, okra and corn-on-the-cob — get their own lines. Tomatoes (cherry vs round) and shrimp (by size / peeled vs shell) captured in the raw subtree, mapping still pending.
_pending.hs10_seafood_produce_2026_07: Tomato split into round (the standard slicing tomato -> tomato) vs cherry (-> cherry-tomato); roma and grape are distinct HS10 types left for a specialty pass. Shrimp split into peeled/P&D (-> shrimp-pd) vs shell-on across all size grades (-> shrimp & shrimp-head-on, which HS cannot distinguish). Squid isolated from cuttlefish. All from the already-pulled HS10 subtree.
